user_saw: During background reclaim of large expired scratch clones, the Gateway thread spent minutes of CPU and tens of GB of allocation on recursive deletion, competing with chat responsiveness.
summary: Atomically claims each expired scratch directory by rename and moves its recursive inspection and deletion into the existing filesystem worker, leaving expiry, custody and identity decisions on the Gateway thread.
reasoning: Scratch expiry was added by 99ba844a (#193677, 2026-11-05) as paced main-thread streaming deletion, and it has always run on the Gateway thread; this change relocates that work to a worker for a measured performance gain rather than restoring earlier behavior or fixing incorrect results. Per the rubric, improving code that was never faster is not-a-defect, although the cost was user-visible as Gateway load.
